cues: Think of it as Pythagoras with a correction.
At ninety degrees cos A is zero, and it is exactly Pythagoras.
Make A acute and a squared is less than b squared plus c squared.
Make A obtuse: cos A turns negative, the foot D slides outside the base, and a squared becomes bigger.
The same formula covers every case.
